surfaces.part: scattered debris pile (dark fragments, two small clusters)

answer.evidence: The sprite is a loose scatter of small dark fragments about 9 rows tall and 9 px wide. It has no standing volume, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no roof plane. The silhouette widens from 6 to 9 px and then tapers to 1 px, so it reads as flat pieces lying on the floor. There is no vertical front face of 3 or more rows. For a debris kind this is the expected flat scatter, and as a drawing it counts as a flat top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny dark crow-like sprite, smaller than one tile, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. It looks like a near-black silhouette with perhaps 2-3 tones, and about 52% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral. That fits a black-on-dark sticker look with little tint. There is no visible material ramp, no feather grain and no highlight clusters. The references carry far more: the hedge has leaf clumps in several greens, and the well and stall have 5-6 steps with per-element highlights and tinted dark outlines. Even next to the small bench, which is also sparse, the candidate has no visible shading ramp. It is also much smaller and sparser than any reference prop, so it reads as thinner and flatter than the Beodeul standard.

It has no standing body, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no vertical south face of 3 or more rows. This is consistent with floor debris, which is meant to be flat. The silhouette widens from 6 px to 9 px at row 8 and then narrows to 1 px at row 13, an irregular blob outline with no ellipse lid or rim. With no front face, it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny dark crow sprite, smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. It is mostly a dark purple-grey silhouette with only a few lighter wing and body highlights, roughly 3-4 readable lightness steps against 5-6 on the references (bench wood, well stones, stall). 52% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, which is similar to the bench (44%) but unlike the tinted outlines of the hedge and stall (0-1%). So the outline is mixed, leaning toward a neutral dark line around the shape. The flat dark body, neutral-leaning outline and shallow ramp would still look thinner than the references, so it fails with doubt.
